2027-02-21.title: M'shario Sunday · The Healing of the Paralytic
readings: The song of Moses as a witness
They hear your words but do not do them
Woe to those who call evil good
Signs and wonders by the apostles
While we were still sinners, Christ died for us
Four friends lower the paralytic through the roof
2027-02-21.alt: Third Sunday of the Great Fast.
theo: Jesus is teaching in a crowded house in Capernaum. Four men bring a paralysed friend on a mat, but they cannot get near. So they climb onto the roof, dig through it, and lower him down in front of Jesus. Mark says: “When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’” The faith of the friends opens the way for the sick man.

Everyone expected a healing of the legs. Jesus begins with the heart. The deepest paralysis is sin: it keeps us from walking towards God and towards others. The scribes object: “Who can forgive sins but God alone?” They are right; and that is exactly the point. Jesus then says: “So that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins… stand up, take your mat and go to your home.” The visible healing proves the invisible one.

Ezekiel warns of people who listen to the prophet's words like a lovely song and do nothing: “they hear what you say, but they will not do it.” Isaiah cries: “Ah, you who call evil good and good evil.” The paralysis of the soul often begins there: hearing without doing, calling sin by softer names. Lent is the time to stand up and walk.

St Paul gives the reason for our hope: “God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us.” We do not have to cure ourselves first. Like the paralytic, we only need to be brought to Jesus, and to let others carry us when we cannot walk.
conn: The four friends are an image of the Church: we carry one another to Christ by prayer, intercession and example.
Christ gave this authority to the apostles (John 20:22–23); it continues in the sacrament of Penance.
Ezekiel 33:32 and James 1:22: be doers of the word, not hearers only.
Acts 5:15: the sick are laid on mats in the street so Peter's shadow may fall on them; Christ's healing continues through the Church.
altar: At every Holy Qurbono we are like the paralytic, lowered before the Lord by the prayer of the whole Church. Before Communion the priest prays for the forgiveness of our sins; then the Lord says to us, “Stand up and walk.”
outline: The roof broken open: what would we do to bring a friend to Jesus?
Point 2 · Sin is the deepest paralysis
Ezekiel and Isaiah: honesty about sin.
Confession and a new start; God loved us while we were sinners.
live: Pray every day this week for one person who cannot or will not come to God.
Choose one teaching from today's Gospel and act on it this week.
If you have not yet confessed this Lent, do it this week.
fathers: How great is the Lord, who for the merit of some pardons others… If you doubt your own merit, seek the prayers of others; the Church will pray for you (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 5, 11).
He sees in the paralytic the human race, made helpless by sin, which the Physician raised by a word, showing that he who forgives is God (Commentary on the Diatessaron).
magis: Only God forgives sins; Jesus, the Son of God, exercises this divine power and gives it to his apostles for the Church.
Christ, physician of souls and bodies, healed the paralytic and forgave his sins; the Church continues this in Penance.
Intercessory prayer: asking on behalf of another, as the four friends did.
saints: 22 Feb: the Throne of St Peter at Antioch. 23 Feb: St Polycarp of Smyrna. 24 Feb: the Finding of the Head of St John the Baptist. 25 Feb: Blessed Rani Maria (as in the 2025–26 lectionary).
2027-02-21.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of four friends and forgave the sins of the paralytic. Forgive our sins, heal the paralysis of our hearts, and make us friends who carry others to you. Raise us up, that we may walk in your ways. Amen.

quick: Four friends carry the paralytic to Jesus: we carry each other by faith.
Jesus heals the deepest paralysis first: sin.
Don't only hear the Word; do it.
2027-02-21.action: Pray daily this week for one person who is far from God.
2027-02-21.question: Whom am I carrying to Jesus, and who is carrying me?
2027-02-21.special: M'shario Sunday, third Sunday of the Great Fast.
illus: When a young man in a Kerala parish was bedridden after an accident, his prayer group came every Friday evening, carried him to the car and took him to the adoration chapel. He says their faith kept his alive. They were the four friends of Capernaum.

family.explain: Four friends carried a man who could not walk to Jesus. The house was full, so they made a hole in the roof! Jesus forgave his sins and healed him.
family.intention: We pray for people who cannot walk or are sick in bed, and for friends who are far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we help a friend to come closer to Jesus?”

kidsaint: A Franciscan Clarist sister from Pulluvazhy in Kerala who worked for poor village families in Madhya Pradesh and was killed in 1995. Her killer later repented, and her family forgave him. Lesson: love and forgiveness can heal hearts.
term: M'shario refers to the paralytic, the man who was “loosed” and raised up. The third Sunday of the Great Fast reads his healing (Mark 2:1–12).
termMore: On the weekdays of the Great Fast the Malankara tradition prays with prostrations (kneeling and bowing to the ground), a bodily sign of repentance. They are not made on the Fortieth Friday and on feast days, as the lectionary notes.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, imagine the scene in Capernaum. Jesus is teaching in a house so crowded that no one can get to the door. Four men arrive carrying a friend who cannot walk. What do they do? They climb onto the roof, dig a hole, and lower their friend down right in front of Jesus. They would not give up.

St Mark says: “When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’” Their faith. Sometimes we cannot bring ourselves to God; others must carry us. And sometimes we are called to carry others: a son who has left the Church, a friend in addiction, a neighbour in despair. Our prayer can open the roof.

Everyone expected Jesus to heal the man's legs. He began with his sins. The deepest paralysis is not in our legs but in our hearts: sin keeps us from walking towards God and others. Only God can forgive sins, said the scribes. Exactly. And to show that he has that authority, Jesus told the man: “Stand up, take your mat and go home.”

Ezekiel warns of people who hear God's word like a beautiful song and then do nothing. Let us not be like that this Lent. Let us make a good Confession, so that we hear Jesus say: “Your sins are forgiven.” And let us become the four friends who carry others to him. Amen.
kids: Children, four friends wanted to bring their friend who could not walk to Jesus. But the house was full of people!
So they climbed onto the roof, made a hole, and lowered their friend down on a mat right in front of Jesus! Jesus forgave his sins and said: “Stand up and walk!” And he walked!
Good friends help each other come to Jesus. Let's say: “Jesus, help me to be a good friend!”

intro: A paralysed man cannot reach Jesus by himself. Four friends carry him, break open a roof and lower him down. Jesus sees their faith, forgives the man's sins and raises him up.

sub: Aaron and Hur held up the weary hands of Moses until the battle was won.
Four friends carry the paralytic and find a way through the roof.
The Church is a community where we carry one another to Jesus by prayer and help.
q: Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side; so his hands were steady until the sun set.
And when they could not bring him to Jesus because of the crowd, they removed the roof above him; and after having dug through it, they let down the mat on which the paralytic lay.
points.apply: Carry one person to Jesus this week: pray for them by name and help them practically.

sub: Jesus first says: “Son, your sins are forgiven.” The deepest paralysis is sin.
The Psalmist blesses God who forgives all iniquity and heals all diseases.
In the sacrament of Reconciliation Christ still speaks these words through his priest.
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits—who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Thank God for the times he has forgiven you, and forgive someone who has hurt you.

sub: God takes no pleasure in the death of the sinner, but wants him to turn and live.
Jesus shows his authority: “Stand up, take your mat and go to your home.”
The healed man walks out before all; forgiveness gives new life and new strength for daily duties.
q: As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live.
“I say to you, stand up, take your mat and go to your home.” And he stood up, and immediately took the mat and went out before all of them.
points.apply: Take up one duty you have been avoiding at home, and do it with new heart.

concl: Faith carried the man, mercy forgave him, power raised him.
Let us be friends who carry others, sinners who accept forgiveness, and disciples who rise and walk.
2027-02-21.resolve: Pray each day this week for one person who is spiritually or physically “paralysed”.
